newsitem.title: USA: IMF releases new funds for Russia.
newsitem.headline: IMF releases new funds for Russia.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Friday approved the resumption of lending to Russia, ordering the release of $647.2 million to the country as a result of tough action it took to revamp its struggling economy.

It approved the funding on the basis of the country achieving monetary and fiscal targets for last December as well as the continued appropriate conduct of credit policy and efforts to improve tax collection, the IMF said in a statement.
It also cited "several important structural reform measures" as reason to release the funds, which are equal to roughly two monthly tranches under the programme.
The IMF delayed payment of several tranches of a $10 billion standby loan agreement made between it and Russia last year, in part because the country had been slow to meet its reform commitments.
It had stalled on making payments under the loan because tax revenues were well below budgeted levels, threatening to undermine government finances, among other factors.

Russia had also acted to recently restructure its economy in the face of stiff domestic opposition. It scrapped plans for quotas on vodka imports, introducing a simple lincensing procedure to register imports.

In addition, it adopted a new pricing procudure for natural gas sales and sharply cut back on the list of so-called strategic consumers of energy whose supplies cannot be cut off even if they fail to pay their bills.
